summary: Ray arrives at a warehouse-like section of a ship where security is tense after the imminent detention of Lilaiken suspects. Armed security officers and then Marine guards posted outside Section 944 stop him; a Marine sergeant named Kilgore checks his card and says Chief Becker wants him to report first. Ray asks for the ground-level truth, and Kilgore's wary reaction and a joke about 'sir' show Ray's cover is strained. The passage ends with Kilgore asking whether Ray is with the FSA or the International Intelligence Agency.
one_line: Ray, posing as a hardware technician, is challenged by Marine guards outside Section 944 and asked whether he works for the FSA or the International Intelligence Agency.
key_facts: Ray is walking through a warehouse district of a ship, a space populated by drone rats and occasional security sweepers.
The imminent detention, interrogation and voiding into space of Lilaiken suspects is the situation putting the speaker in a foul mood.
Security officers, called sec-os, are carrying firearms, which they normally do not do because passenger classes find armed crewmen disconcerting.
Two Marine guards with rifles are stationed outside the bulkhead door to Section 944.
The Marine sergeant at the door has a badge identifying him as Kilgore and sergeant's stripes on his arm.
Kilgore asks for Ray's ID; Ray shows his card and gives a stupid grin like the one in the photo on it.
Kilgore says Chief Becker said Ray should report to him before poking around.
Ray asks what is going on, wanting the bareboned, clinical report one Marine gives another rather than the security spin.
When Ray says 'sir' to Kilgore, Kilgore responds 'Don't call me sir, Marine,' an old basic training joke.
Ray is dressed in rat-related gear and hardware geek coveralls, which Kilgore looks him over in.
Kilgore finally asks whether Ray is 'Smith or Jones,' meaning FSA or International Intelligence Agency.
